chapter: Childhood in Tyler, Beaumont and Houston
title: Learning the bass drum part and marching in his first parade
summary: Bonomo showed him the bass drum notes; he filled in one night and then played the bass drum on a wagon in a parade, his first playing with a group.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Yeah.
And --
You mean, you could hear the music as well or just the --
I heard the music. I couldn't read nothing. I just went along.
Yeah, yeah.

And so, one night, the one that played the bass drum, he wasn't there. And Joe showed me, he said, "This note is for the bass drum, and these are the notes I play because I'm playing the snare drum, like that."
Yeah.
And when they would play a number, I
would notice each the beat.
Yeah.
That they was playing.
Those whole notes.
That's right, for the bass drum.
Yeah.
See, it would be an eighth note and a --
Yeah, right.
Do a --
So you were both watching on the same piece of music?
Oh, yes, I would be standing right there watching.
Yeah.
But I just really learned the numbers without knowing exactly about the beats.
Yeah.
And so I sat in and played the bass drum that night. And I was watching, and I know how the song go.
Yeah.
I knew it.
That's right. And you had those notes to guide you.
That's right. And that's the way I
then learned to play:
That's fascinating. You must have been very excited when you first --

Oh, yes, I went home and I told my mother I played the drums with the band. And she didn't want to believe it, until he they came over and told her. And the bass drum player couldn't make it. They had a parade one day. And I was in the parade, and they had someone to pull the bass drum and I played the bass drum, walking down the street.
It was on someone else's back?
No, they had it on a wagon, a little wagon.
And they pulled it and you --
And I played it, I sure did.
Did you hit it from one side only?
One side only, see. And that was really my very first time playing with any group at all.
And you were about nine by then?
Oh, yeah. I loved that.
Isn't that terrific?
And --
Oh, that was a big thrill.
Big thrill for me.
And marching in time.
Sure, and my mother came down to see
me, watching.
And I guess that gave you a little prestige in school, didn't it?
Oh, sure, yeah, yeah.
All the kids saw you.
That's right, that's right, they saw me. And then --
Well, he was a nice man, then.
Very nice man. And he turned out to be --
Did he have any kids?
No, he didn't. He turned out to be a comedian, also.
Did he?
And I saw him again in Houston, Texas. So --
That's --
He always was with a show at the time. And he was a very funny guy.
Oh, isn't that good?
